transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Yeah, nice to meet you too. Um, so I guess the main thing that pushed me to come in is... well, it's work. I process insurance claims, and I just keep getting up from my workstation during the day. Even when I know I’m supposed to stay put and finish my claim reviews, I just... I don't know, I get up. 

Like on Tuesday, I got up and ended up in the breakroom talking to Dave from accounting. Dave's a great guy, he actually just got this new golden retriever puppy, and he was showing me pictures on his phone for a while. I've always wanted a dog, you know? But my apartment building has this super strict no-pets policy, which is ridiculous because they charge so much for rent and the plumbing is honestly terrible. The sink in my bathroom has been leaking for a month and maintenance won't even call me back. 

But... wait, sorry, what was I saying? Oh, right, work. Yeah, I just can't seem to stay in my seat to actually finish my work when I'm supposed to.
Have you struggled with staying focused and sitting still like this since you were a child, or is this something that has only started happening more recently?

Um, yeah, looking back, this definitely isn't a brand new thing for me. Like, in elementary school, my teachers used to always write on my report cards that I was a bright kid, but... well, actually, my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she was the best. She used to hand out these scratch-and-sniff stickers if you did a good job. The grape ones were amazing. I actually tried to buy some of those online the other day, just for the nostalgia, you know? But shipping has been so weird lately. Half my packages keep ending up at my neighbor's door, and he gets so mad about it. He's this older guy who already complains if my TV is even slightly too loud, so having to knock on his door to get my mail is just super awkward... 

Wait, sorry, what was the question? Oh, right, childhood. Yeah, so my teachers would say I was bright, but they were always writing notes home that I lost my worksheets or completely missed the instructions. They constantly had to give me reminders just to actually finish my classwork.

Beyond getting up from your desk, do you often feel like you have an internal motor that makes you feel restless or unable to sit still for long periods, like when you are watching a movie or sitting in a meeting?

Um, an internal motor? No, I don't think so. I don't really feel restless inside like that. Like, I can sit through a whole movie just fine. Actually, I just went to the theater last weekend to see that new sci-fi movie that just came out. The CGI was pretty incredible, but man, the seats at the theater near my place are just the absolute worst. They supposedly just renovated the whole building, but they didn't even put in those nice reclining seats, you know? 

My buddy Mark just bought one of those big leather recliners for his apartment, the kind with the built-in cup holders and the USB chargers in the armrest. We watched the game at his place on Sunday and he made these amazing jalapeño poppers from scratch. I tried to ask him for the recipe, but he said it's a family secret, which is honestly kind of dumb because I'm pretty sure he just found it on TikTok. I've been trying to cook more at home lately to save money, but groceries are just so expensive right now... 

Wait, sorry, I lost my train of thought. What were we talking about? Did you ask me something about movies?
When you are in situations where you need to be quiet, like in a library or during a serious conversation, do you often find yourself talking excessively or interrupting others?

Um, talking excessively? No, not really. I mean, I don't think I interrupt people or talk too much when I'm supposed to be quiet. Like, if I'm at the library, I'm pretty good about keeping it down. Actually, I used to go to the library all the time when I was taking classes at the community college. They had this really great coffee shop right on the first floor. It was super convenient, but their espresso machine was broken half the time. 

It was so frustrating because I really need my caffeine, especially in the mornings. I tried making cold brew at home for a while, but I could never get the ratio right. It always came out tasting super bitter or way too watered down. My sister makes the best cold brew, but she uses these special beans she orders from Portland. She's actually moving there next month, which is crazy because she's never even visited Oregon before. She just packed up her whole life and decided to go. I helped her pack her apartment last weekend, and we found all this stuff from when we were kids...

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. Um, what did you ask me? Something about the library? No, I don't really talk too much in quiet places.
